title: DepsRAG: Towards Agentic Reasoning and Planning for Software Dependency Management
datasets: Chainlit v1.1.200 dependency graph (built via Deps.Dev API)
metrics: Cypher query correctness; number of query retries; percentage of correct answers
evaluation_design: ablation study (with vs. without Critic-Agent); case study on a single package dependency graph; evaluation with two LLMs on three multi-step reasoning tasks
limitations: evaluated on a single package and version (Chainlit 1.1.200); only three multi-step reasoning questions; no formal statistical testing; relies on external Deps.Dev API for dependency data
open_challenges: complex hierarchical dependency structure complicates standard RAG; decomposing tasks into sub-tasks and extracting relevant graph information; aggregating data from heterogeneous sources; routing and delegation while avoiding infinite loops and deadlocks; validating the final response and refining queries for better KG retrieval
agentic_evidence: Four agents (AssistantAgent, DependencyGraphAgent, SearchAgent, CriticAgent) exchange routed messages; the Agent-Critic loop iteratively refines answers until the Critic endorses the output.
architecture_notes: Langroid-based multi-agent orchestration; AssistantAgent decomposes queries and routes via QuestionTool/ForwardTool; DependencyGraphAgent builds and queries a Neo4j dependency KG (ConstructKGTool, GraphSchemaTool, CypherQueryTool); SearchAgent uses WebSearchTool and VulnerabilityTool; CriticAgent gives feedback in a loop.
result_summary: Threefold increase in answer accuracy with the Critic-Agent loop; GPT-4-Turbo generated correct Cypher queries on the first attempt for all questions, while Llama-3 needed retries and produced one incorrect answer.

metrics: relative performance improvement

architecture_notes: Two-step pipeline: (1) unsupervised BERT-like joint API embedding model (subword + word Transformer encoders, three pre-training tasks) ranks target APIs by usage/name similarity; (2) mapped API names are inserted into a prompt template that guides the LLM to generate target API code.
result_summary: HaPiM improves API migration over directly querying LLMs by 43.7% (cross-library) and 27.4% (cross-language), and outperforms existing API migration approaches.

title: Qiskit Code Migration with LLMs
datasets: automatically generated taxonomy of Qiskit migration scenarios; synthetic Python Qiskit code snippets; Qiskit release notes
metrics: stoplight metrics (X, X+, OK-, OK); expected scenarios detected (P perf.); detected vs expected scenario ratio (P glob.); invocation failure rate

limitations: evaluation restricted to synthetic Python snippets; no realistic whole-project migration; small number of runs and LLMs; no significance testing of model/retrieval differences; single quantum ecosystem (Qiskit)
open_challenges: expand knowledge base with changelogs and official migration guides; migrate real public-repository projects instead of snippets; automated syntactic/semantic validation and test generation; define precise code-migration quality metrics; evaluate ecosystem-specialised models

title: Agentic Generation of AST Transformation Rules for Fixing Breaking Updates
metrics: compilable transformation rate; fix rate; cross-project fix rate
evaluation_design: benchmark evaluation on 157 breaking dependency updates; eight (LLM, AST engine) configurations; cross-project transfer validation set
limitations: agent may apply direct edits instead of producing a structured transformation; agent may stop autonomously leaving malformed transformations; documentation navigation chosen to avoid context saturation
open_challenges: transfer success depends on usage uniformity across clients; AST transformation engine API complexity determines compilation success
agentic_evidence: coding agent through a generate-apply-verify loop: the agent builds the transformation against an AST transformation engine, applies it to the broken client until success based on compiler feedback, then deploys it over other clients
architecture_notes: Four-step workflow: input context assembly (client project, engine Javadoc, transformation template, dependency API spec/Javadoc), agentic generation and application, isolated transformation verification, and cross-project transfer.
result_summary: Best configuration reaches 94.3% compilable transformation rate and 78.6% fix rate; transformations transfer across projects with a 33.3% cross-project fix rate overall and 80% or above for updates with uniform API usage.
